title: Prove a one-sided connector barrier and certify a full escape word
body:
This **scoped theorem** excludes any star caller whose thin connectors have identical columns on three leaves, or identical rows on three leaves. It holds for every finite port dimension, every full-rank orthogonal stage split, every call order, and any number or rank of thin connectors in characteristic two. **Complete kappa is unchanged.**

[Proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c10f75f09e41803ae8efe478331a7509b7379b2f/research/crossed-connector-caller/PROOF.md), [exact evidence](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c10f75f09e41803ae8efe478331a7509b7379b2f/research/crossed-connector-caller/RESULT.json), [full escape word](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c10f75f09e41803ae8efe478331a7509b7379b2f/research/crossed-connector-caller/ESCAPE-WORD.json), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c10f75f09e41803ae8efe478331a7509b7379b2f/research/crossed-connector-caller/SOURCES.json).

The proof replaces an order census by a prefix identity. The forbidden chronology would give the same determinant both `(1+x)^(3d)` and `(1+x)^d`. Thus adding more pooled queries or more stage splits cannot repair the contract. The resulting signature and rank cut identifies a concrete remaining target: 31 leaves with five rank-two connectors. The corresponding one-port budget is excluded; coupling pairs of ports passes this necessary cut. Its optimistic pinned P104 price is positive at saving `.0035`, but **no such long word or native supplier is supplied**.

A different, complete eight-field binary word does escape the obstruction. It has six full calls and eight thin queries. Every polynomial coefficient passes, but its fixed P104 linear margin is `-336`, and a separated-rank argument rejects every concave moment. A saved counterexample passes the pure stage word and first mixed coefficients but fails higher coefficients. These distinguish a real operator from an insufficient screen.

The separate checker uses no solver or discovery module. Normal and optimized registered checks, five corrupted-package controls, committed-byte checks, and read-only Git-free replay pass. It checks the full escape word, fifteen small paired-order identities, coupled chronology, prefix determinants, and exact integer-power prices. The archive also preserves changed query frames, coupled five-query searches, and four failed fixed-source growth attempts. Timeouts remain unknown; no search failure is used as a universal proof.

Base and refreshed canonical main: `df0137efd35e11b4445734bf612bdd4c7ebc330c`, priority seven, selected kappa `.00310045`. Contribution head: `c10f75f09e41803ae8efe478331a7509b7379b2f`. The bill is frozen at [PR #5599](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5599), source `09dd0965711ca7eeb169057a420abab1c9052137`. This does not change the frontier.

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds.git 0c27282f56a0e8ec6c1fbad0f2ccca646d0d8442
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/crossed-connector-caller
```

Expected: `PASS_ONE_SIDED_CONNECTOR_OBSTRUCTION` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Python 3.12 and the standard library suffice. The fetch supplies an explicitly pinned open provenance object. A full ancestry audit was not run because that source is not an ancestor of the new main base. Hosted CI and independent scientific review are separate statuses. No characteristic-zero reduction, native frame admission, ownership/tape realization, full compiler/outer transfer, or proof-assistant acceptance is claimed.

Credit Cinna Davis's controller/simplex work, [PR #5617](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5617), [PR #5631](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5631), and [PR #5649](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5649). Retain the P104 helper and contact lineage, Gareth Davidson, David Arias, Jacob Alan Sussman, zxv, Cao Yifan, and all pinned source notices. The vendored discovery alphabet retains Cinna Davis's notice. Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. Apache-2.0.
